text: rwb-integration runs as its own ACE database login with grants on its own schema rwb_integration only (DP-02), replacing the shared recovery service identity of the legacy story, and the booking-confirmation workflow, its activities and its rerun all run under that one login carried by the chart as a secret reference.
why: No source document names the per-service login, while DP-02 requires one login per service and Architecture v5 slides 16 and 41 give rwb-integration its own schema, topic and task queue.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 16 and 41; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-02; Ownership Map schema row rwb_integration; legacy RWB-E2-007 sections 10 and 13 (the recovery service identity).
applied_in: 3 Preconditions, 10 Authority and 13 Solution plan of RWB-P2-E2007-APP
confirm: ACE team and DBA (schema and login provisioning, RWB-PLT-DB)
impact: The story builds and tests against the rwb-integration login once it is allocated; no behaviour of the match changes.

text: JOB-08 Booking confirmation and its activities belong to rwb-integration in this realignment, as RWB-P4-E2007-APP and RWB-ITG-E2007-ITG both state, and the job is an event-started workflow on AceDataReady with no Schedule; the Architecture v5 slide 44 row that names rwb-payment as its owner is recorded as superseded for this job.
why: Two sources disagree: Architecture v5 slide 44 names rwb-payment the owner of JOB-08 and slides 42 and 43 do not list rwb-integration among the consumers of AceDataReady or TreatmentApproved, while the accepted split of this legacy key places the match in rwb-integration.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 42, 43 and 44; RWB-P4-E2007-APP section 1; RWB-ITG-E2007-ITG sections 1, 12.5 and 19; RWB-P3-E2007-APP section 12.6; Template and Rules v1 R3 and R5.5 DP-10.
applied_in: 1 Story, 2 Business rationale, 3 Preconditions, 8 BR14, 12.4, 12.6 and 13 of RWB-P2-E2007-APP
confirm: Solution architect owns the ruling; platform workflow kit owner and the rwb-payment owner accept it
impact: The workflow runs on the rwb-integration queue and the job catalogue row is written there; no Schedule is created and the rwb-payment slice of JOB-08 is not built.

text: Only rwb-source-data reads the recovery.v_ace_* views and ACE data; the accounts and their booked terms, the ALS batch-completeness answer and the REC-03 write of this key all go through the rwb-source-data contract, TSD P2 Integration v3 T5.2 is superseded on its direct-read sentence, and rwb_integration holds no grant on recovery and no view of its own.
why: ADR-010, DP-05 and Architecture v5 slides 41 and 45 make rwb-source-data the only reader of the ACE views, while TSD P2 Integration v3 T5.2 states that P2 reads the views in T1.1 directly; the higher source wins and the loser is recorded.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 8, 9, 13, 29, 37, 41 and 45; ADR-010; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-05; TSD P2 Integration v3 T5.2; FSD P2 Integration v3 A1.1 and A1.4.
applied_in: 2 Business rationale, 3 Preconditions, 8 BR12, 11 Data, 12.2 and 17 of RWB-P2-E2007-APP
confirm: Solution architect; the rwb-source-data and rwb-integration owners; ACE team
impact: The match reads the ACE facts through a contract with a 2 s budget instead of a view; the ACE team grants no SELECT on recovery to rwb_integration.

text: The six consumed calls that no source gives an HTTP path or a JSON shape — the approved-not-booked treatment list, the mark-booked write, the booking-difference write, the case-account read at a business date, the REC-03 reconciliation write and the rwb-case task raise — carry the placeholder in the story and are taken from RWB-P3-E2004-CON, RWB-P1-E2007-APP and the rwb-case contract when they are published; the rerun of a job in this service's catalogue is served on the integration base at POST /admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun.
why: The legacy story names these calls as Java interfaces only, and the generic rerun of the job catalogue is kept with P1 in API Specification v4 and the Ownership Map while a rwb-integration job can only be rerun by rwb-integration.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-007 sections 12 and 13; Ownership Map API rows POST /admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun (owner P1) and GET /admin/scheduled-jobs (owner P2); TSD P2 Integration v3 Appendix T-A API-P2-009; RWB-P2-E2007-CON section 12.2.
applied_in: 11 Data, 12.1, 12.2 and 13 of RWB-P2-E2007-APP
confirm: Contract owners of rwb-treatment, rwb-source-data and rwb-case; solution architect for the rerun placement
impact: The paths and field names are confirmed or corrected in the owning contract baselines; the workflow and its fakes follow the correction without a behaviour change.

text: MSG-P1-001 uses the FSD P2 Integration v3 wording '{product} is from {date}. Today's data is not yet complete.' in place of the legacy 'Today's load has not arrived.', and every other message of this key keeps its legacy or platform text unchanged.
why: The legacy story carries one wording and the current FSD carries the reworded text after D-RCV-35; the FSD is the higher source for a message text and the change is recorded rather than silent.
read: FSD P2 Integration v3 VR-P2-001-1 and the version 3 change note; legacy RWB-E2-007 section 14; Template and Rules v1 R3 and R7.3.
applied_in: 14 Validation and messages of RWB-P2-E2007-APP
confirm: Platform message catalogue owner; business analyst of P2
impact: Only the batch-gate message text changes; no test value and no scenario changes.

text: Package BOOKING_MATCH, its version BKG-2026.12, its RESTRUCTURE and SETTLEMENT rows and the tolerance of 0.00 baht are kept as the legacy values of this key, and the row identifiers of the package stay in the rwb-decision registry and are named by no source of this story, so the criteria cite the outcome and the version only.
why: The legacy values are fixed by D-RCV-36 and the story master, the registry rows are rwb-decision's, and inventing a row identifier would breach the rule that no value is invented.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-007 sections 3, 7 and 8; D-RCV-36 T3 and T5; ADR-012; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 27; Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 15.
applied_in: 3 Preconditions, 7 Acceptance criteria, 8 BR10 and 18 Traceability of RWB-P2-E2007-APP
confirm: RW-COE with the registry owner (RWB-P7-E2007-APP, RWB-E2-042)
impact: The evaluation names the fired row and the version at run time; the story asserts the outcome and the version and needs no row identifier.

text: rwb-integration subscribes to rwb.source-data.AceDataReady.v1 and rwb.treatment.TreatmentApproved.v1 as an additional consumer for the JOB-08 run, deduplicated through its own processed_event inbox, although Architecture v5 slides 42 and 43 do not list it in those consumer lists.
why: The run cannot start without AceDataReady and the legacy listener holds the approval date from TreatmentApproved, while the event catalogue consumer lists were written before this realignment placed JOB-08 here.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 42 and 43 (EV-26 and EV-10 consumer lists); legacy RWB-E2-007 sections 4 and 12 (TreatmentApprovedListener, events consumed); Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-09.
applied_in: 12.3, 12.4 and 13 of RWB-P2-E2007-APP
confirm: Event catalogue owner (RWB-PLT-EVT) and the producers rwb-source-data and rwb-treatment
impact: Two consumer rows are added to the catalogue and the service registers one consumer group; no producer changes.

text: No data lake exists in the target (DP-17): nothing in this key builds, sends or reads a lake file, and the REC-03 result reaches reporting as a row of the rwb-source-data reconciliation answer and from there as events.
why: Architecture v5 slide 37 and DP-17 remove the data lake, while the legacy module owned lake extracts; the key must be explicit that no lake artefact survives.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 37; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-17; FSD P2 Integration v3 A1.5 and A1.6.
applied_in: 2 Business rationale, 8 BR16, 12.9 and 19 of RWB-P2-E2007-APP
confirm: Solution architect; rwb-reporting owner
impact: No lake job, file or connection is built for this key; REC-03 is read from the reconciliation answer and published as events.

text: The contract baseline records JOB-08 as a rwb-integration job started by AceDataReady with no Schedule, accepts the two added consumer rows, and records the Architecture v5 slide 44 owner row of rwb-payment as superseded for this job rather than leaving the seam ambiguous.
why: Architecture v5 slide 44 names rwb-payment the owner of JOB-08 and the event catalogue lists no rwb-integration consumer row, while RWB-P4-E2007-APP, RWB-ITG-E2007-ITG and RWB-P2-E2007-APP all place the match in rwb-integration.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 42, 43 and 44; RWB-P4-E2007-APP section 1; RWB-ITG-E2007-ITG sections 12.5 and 19; Template and Rules v1 R3 and R5.5 DP-10.
applied_in: 1 Story, 8 BR5 and BR9, 12.4, 12.6 and 13 of RWB-P2-E2007-CON
confirm: Solution architect; the rwb-payment owner and the event catalogue owner
impact: The contract fixes the trigger, the task queue and the two subscriptions once, and every consumer of the baseline builds against them.

text: rwb-integration serves POST /api/recovery/integration/v1/admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun for the jobs of its own catalogue, under the Platform administration U right and an Idempotency-Key per job and business date, while the generic rerun row of API Specification v4 and the Ownership Map stays with P1 for the other services' jobs; the client identity is the rwb-integration login (DP-02).
why: The legacy story names the rerun at that path, API Specification v4 and the Ownership Map keep the path with x-module P1, and only the service that owns a job can rerun its workflow; no source names the login the callers authenticate as.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-007 section 12; Ownership Map API row POST /admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun (owner P1) and table job_catalog (owner P2); TSD P2 Integration v3 Appendix T-A API-P2-009; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-13.
applied_in: 10 Authority, 12.1 and 14 of RWB-P2-E2007-CON
confirm: Solution architect; the rwb-source-data and rwb-integration owners; platform administrator
impact: The rerun is served once per service for its own jobs; the catalogue read stays the base's surface and the P1 row keeps the other services' jobs.

text: The twelve consumed operations are declared with the element names this contract fixes, the five unsettled paths and shapes carry the placeholder, and the account fact and batch answer are consumed from rwb-source-data with TSD P2 Integration v3 T5.2 recorded as superseded; rwb_integration holds no grant on recovery.
why: The sources name the legacy Java interfaces and LDM field IDs, not the JSON property names or HTTP paths of the target contracts, and TSD P2 v3 T5.2 contradicts ADR-010 and DP-05 on the ACE read.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-007 sections 11 and 12; TSD P2 Integration v3 T5.2 and T3.1; ADR-010; Ownership Map API rows GET /data-products/freshness and GET /treatments/{treatmentId}; Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8 (DF-TRT, DF-ACE, DF-ACC, DF-WRK, DF-OPS and DF-DEC ranges).
applied_in: 11 Data, 12.2, 12.8 and 17 of RWB-P2-E2007-CON
confirm: Contract owners of rwb-treatment, rwb-source-data, rwb-case, rwb-decision and rwb-access
impact: The names are confirmed or corrected in the owning baselines; the fakes and the app story follow the correction without a behaviour change.

text: The two consumer rows of AceDataReady and TreatmentApproved are additive rows of the event catalogue for the booking-confirmation consumer group of rwb-integration, and neither event's producer, payload or key changes.
why: The run cannot start and cannot hold the approval date without the two events, while Architecture v5 slides 42 and 43 list other consumers only.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 42 and 43; legacy RWB-E2-007 sections 4 and 12; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-09.
confirm: Event catalogue owner (RWB-PLT-EVT); rwb-source-data and rwb-treatment owners
impact: One consumer group is registered; the producers and the two topics are unchanged.

text: MSG-P1-001 uses the FSD P2 Integration v3 wording in the contract and in every alert, the other six messages keep their legacy and platform texts, the package row identifiers stay in the rwb-decision registry, and the contract cites no row identifier of its own.
why: The legacy and the FSD give different texts for MSG-P1-001, and the package rows are rwb-decision's, so a contract that named a row identifier would fix a value another owner holds.
read: FSD P2 Integration v3 VR-P2-001-1; legacy RWB-E2-007 section 14; D-RCV-36 T3 and T5; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 27.
applied_in: 8 BR13, 12.2, 14 and 18 of RWB-P2-E2007-CON
confirm: Platform message catalogue owner; RW-COE with the registry owner
impact: The message map and the task table are final; the registry keeps the row identifiers and the version.

text: The release registers BookingMatchWorkflow and its six activities on the rwb-integration task queue in namespace rwb-recovery as an event-started workflow of AceDataReady, creates no Schedule for JOB-08, and records the Architecture v5 slide 44 owner row of rwb-payment as superseded for this job.
why: Architecture v5 slide 44 names rwb-payment the owner of JOB-08 and slides 42 and 43 list no rwb-integration consumer row, while the accepted split of this legacy key registers the workflow here; a release that shipped either reading silently would leave the run unstarted or doubled.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 42, 43 and 44; Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 27; RWB-PLT-E1071-CON; RWB-P2-E2007-APP section 12.6.
applied_in: 1 Story, 4 Flow, 8 BR3, 12.5, 12.6 and 13 of RWB-P2-E2007-OPS
confirm: Solution architect; platform workflow kit owner; the rwb-payment owner
impact: The registration check asserts the queue, the seven registrations and the event start, and asserts that no Schedule exists.

text: The four alert thresholds, the aggregation window of the four dashboard series and the run-window expectation that triggers the late-batch alert are values of the environment and are reviewed with the business on-call owner, not fixed in code, a chart template or a document.
why: No source fixes any threshold, window or dimension of this run, and the legacy story only names the measure REC-03 and the two task messages.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-007 sections 2, 5 and 16; FSD P2 Integration v3 A1.4; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 41 and 42; ADR-023; Template and Rules v1 R7.2 s17.
applied_in: 11 Data, 13 Solution plan and 14 of RWB-P2-E2007-OPS
confirm: Business on-call owner (RW-COE) and the observability owner (RWB-PLT-OBS)
impact: Each environment tunes its own thresholds; the alert rules, the message IDs and the runbook links do not change.

text: The four runbook entries — event not received or worker not polling, missing-booking wave, terms wave, and no package in force with a late ACE batch — are owned by the DevOps team for the platform steps and by the business on-call owner for the package steps, and are reviewed by the on-call rota before promotion.
why: No source names the runbook entries, their owners or their review cycle, and an alert without an owned entry is not operable.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-007 sections 5, 10 and 13; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 44; ADR-023; Template and Rules v1 R7.2 s14.
applied_in: 10 Authority, 11 Data, 13 Solution plan and 15 of RWB-P2-E2007-OPS
confirm: DevOps team; RW-COE; release manager
impact: Each alert links one owned entry, and the runbook review is a promotion gate rather than a post-release task.

text: The release carries the rwb-integration login as a secret reference from the platform secret store, polls the rwb-integration task queue only and requests no grant on recovery or on another rwb_* schema.
why: No source names the login, the secret reference or the worker identity of rwb-integration under DP-02, while the platform rules require one login per service and one task queue per service.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 16 and 41; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-02 and DP-10; Ownership Map schema row rwb_integration; legacy RWB-E2-007 section 10.
applied_in: 3 Preconditions, 10 Authority and 12.7 of RWB-P2-E2007-OPS
confirm: ACE team and DBA (RWB-PLT-DB); platform administrator
impact: The release is provisioned once the login is allocated; the readiness probe names the first successful authorise call as its dependency check.

text: The build ID is the one the workflow kit supplies for the release commit, worker versioning is enabled so a new build takes new runs while the old build drains, and the payload codec is attached to every client and worker of the deployment.
why: No source fixes the build ID format or the versioning policy, while the workflow kit requires both for a workflow that runs unattended on an event.
read: Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 27; RWB-PLT-E1071-CON; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 24.
applied_in: 12.5 and 13 of RWB-P2-E2007-OPS
confirm: Platform workflow kit owner
impact: An in-flight run finishes on the build that started it, and a rollback redeploys the previous chart with its own build ID.

text: The backfill limit per run and the reuse window of the Idempotency-Key are values of the environment; a date already completed under the same key replays the stored answer, and a treatment that failed on a consumed contract is picked up by the next business date rather than repaired by a script.
why: No source fixes the backfill limit or the key window, while the legacy repeat-run rule (one record and one open task per treatment and date) has to hold for a backfill as well as for an event-started run.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-007 sections 4 and 5 (X5, X6); Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-09; RWB-P2-E2007-CON section 12.1.
applied_in: 5 Exception paths, 8 BR6, 11 Data and 13 of RWB-P2-E2007-OPS
confirm: DevOps team; platform workflow kit owner; the rwb-integration owner
impact: The backfill is safe to repeat and needs no repair script; both values are tuned per environment.

text: MSG-P1-001 uses the FSD P2 Integration v3 wording in the late-batch alert and in the skipped-run message, and the other alert texts are the legacy and platform texts unchanged.
why: The legacy story and the current FSD give different wordings for MSG-P1-001, and an alert must carry the text the catalogue holds.
read: FSD P2 Integration v3 VR-P2-001-1; legacy RWB-E2-007 section 14; Template and Rules v1 R3 and R7.3.
applied_in: 13 Solution plan and 14 of RWB-P2-E2007-OPS
confirm: Platform message catalogue owner; business analyst of P2
impact: Only the batch-gate wording changes; the alert routing and the runbook links are unaffected.
